case.title: Invoiced and Paid work orders show why the lead can't be changed
case.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · about 25 minutes.
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043, v26.40.8-7a95011).
  • [User-A] = you: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit.
  • Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  • One location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); everything below is created in this location.
  • [Tech-A]: one eligible technician at this location. A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • [Tech-B]: a second eligible technician at this location (same rules as [Tech-A]). Their column shows on Board View and their group in Tech View even with no work orders, so the locked work orders can be dragged over it.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip" (used by this case only), with a contact, and two work orders with Lead Technician [Tech-A] set before invoicing: [WO-1] Invoiced and [WO-2] Paid.
  • Names and numbers are examples; what must hold: one Invoiced and one Paid work order, both with a lead.

Setup

  1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  2. Use one location for the whole case: it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  3. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: reuse a technician only after checking it is active, has Time Clock on, a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User and this location in Location; otherwise add one: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as [Tech-A] (e.g. Esther Howard) and [Tech-B] (e.g. Ralph Edwards).
  4. Create the customer used only by this case: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  5. How to reach each status (standard steps): Estimate = a new work order whose lines are not approved. Approved = approve its lines. In Progress = a technician clicks Start time clock on an approved line's Labor row. Review = set the work order to Ready for Review with its status control. Complete = enter a tech story on every line, complete each line, then complete the work order. Invoiced = Finance tab > Create Invoice (the work order needs a contact person). Paid = record a full payment on that invoice. Declined = decline the estimate.
  6. Create these work orders for "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip": Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. The new work order opens with the New Line form (otherwise click New Line on the Lines tab): in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; typed free text finds no results), turn on Line Approved so the work order status reads Approved, and click Save & Close. Write down the number the build gives the work order (on a QA branch they look like "S10043-17581"). Then pick the lead in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once. (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Assign lead technician > click the technician; it is assigned at once.) Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
    • [WO-1] (e.g. S1-511): Lead Technician = [Tech-A], then taken to Invoiced.
    • [WO-2] (e.g. S1-366): Lead Technician = [Tech-A], then taken to Paid.
  7. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > Search "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip" shows [WO-1] (Invoiced) and [WO-2] (Paid), both led by [Tech-A]. If not, fix the status or lead before starting; then clear the search.
case.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and pick Board View in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar; tooltip "Board View").
  2. Type "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip" in Search.
  3. Look at the [WO-1] card and write down any sign that it can only be reordered within its technician (e.g. a lock icon).
  4. Hover the lock icon on the [WO-1] card and read its tooltip.
  5. Hover the card, click More actions and hover the Reassign lead technician action.
  6. Read the tooltip shown next to the Reassign lead technician action.
  7. Hover the Unassign action and read its tooltip.
  8. Press Escape to close the menu.
  9. Drag the [WO-1] card over [Tech-B]'s column and, without releasing it, read the note at the top of [Tech-B]'s column.
  10. Release the card and read which column it is in.
  11. Repeat steps 3 to 10 for [WO-2].
  12. Repeat steps 3 to 11 in Tech View on the rows, dragging each row over [Tech-B]'s group.
case.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The Invoiced and Paid cards and rows carry a lock icon, the visible sign that they can only be reordered within their current technician and not moved to another one.
  • Hovering the lock icon shows the tooltip “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” on [WO-1] and “Paid · can’t be reassigned” on [WO-2].
  • Reassign lead technician and Unassign are shown disabled, and their tooltip reads exactly: Invoiced · can’t be reassigned (on [WO-1]) or Paid · can’t be reassigned (on [WO-2]). (A straight or curly apostrophe is not a difference.)
  • While [WO-1] or [WO-2] is dragged over [Tech-B]'s column or group, the note at its top reads “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” (for [WO-1]) or “Paid · can’t be reassigned” (for [WO-2]).
  • On release the drop is refused: the card or row stays with [Tech-A], and its lead stays [Tech-A].

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S4-N6, S4-N7 and S4-N2, read 19 Oct 2026. PRD §9 User Feedback Summary row "Reassignment not allowed in current status". Design export of 8 Oct 2026 (Claude Design project 787fef1a, Work Orders.dc.html): lock icon next to the number with tooltip "Invoiced · can’t be reassigned" and a locked menu note; since PRD version 68 the PRD uses the same words, and the PRD text is asserted here. Source-verified 19 October 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-N6: “On an Invoiced or Paid work order the Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician action (S3-R14) and the Unassign action are disabled, and their tooltip reads “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” or “Paid · can’t be reassigned”, as in the design. The same words are the tooltip on the card’s or row’s lock icon, and the note shown at the top of another technician’s column or group while the work order is dragged over it, where the drop is refused.”
  • S4-N7: “Visually indicate that an Invoiced or Paid work order can only be reordered within its current technician, not moved to another one.”
  • S4-N2: “Do not allow the lead technician to change in Invoiced or Paid status. An Invoiced or Paid work order can still be dragged to reorder it within its current technician (or within Unassigned), but it cannot be moved to another technician, to Unassigned, or out of Unassigned. Declined and Complete work orders can be moved freely, as today.”

Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

Record them as [Tech-A] (e.g. Esther Howard).
  4. Create the customer used only by this case: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Locked Lead Tooltip" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  5. How to reach each status (standard steps): Estimate = a new work order whose lines are not approved. Approved = approve its lines. Complete = enter a tech story on every line, complete each line, then complete the work order. Invoiced = Finance tab > Create Invoice (the work order needs a contact person). Paid = record a full payment on that invoice. Declined = decline the estimate.

The new work order opens with the New Line form (otherwise click New Line on the Lines tab): in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; typed free text finds no results), turn on Line Approved so the work order status reads Approved, and click Save & Close. Write down the number the build gives the work order (on a QA branch they look like "S10043-17581"). Then pick the lead in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once.     • [WO-1] (e.g. S1-511): Lead Technician = [Tech-A], then taken to Invoiced.

Expected results

  • The Invoiced and Paid cards and rows carry a lock icon, the visible sign that they can only be reordered within their current technician and not moved to another one.
  • Hovering the lock icon shows the tooltip “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” on [WO-1] and “Paid · can’t be reassigned” on [WO-2].
  • Reassign lead technician and Unassign are shown disabled, and their tooltip reads exactly: Invoiced · can’t be reassigned (on [WO-1]) or Paid · can’t be reassigned (on [WO-2]). (A straight or curly apostrophe is not a difference.)
  • While [WO-1] or [WO-2] is dragged over [Tech-B]'s column or group, the note at its top reads “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” (for [WO-1]) or “Paid · can’t be reassigned” (for [WO-2]).
  • On release the drop is refused: the card or row stays with [Tech-A], and its lead stays [Tech-A].

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S4-N6, S4-N7 and S4-N2, read 19 Oct 2026. PRD §9 User Feedback Summary row "Reassignment not allowed in current status". Design export of 8 Oct 2026 (Claude Design project 787fef1a, Work Orders.dc.html): lock icon next to the number with tooltip "Invoiced · can’t be reassigned" and a locked menu note; since PRD version 68 the PRD uses the same words, and the PRD text is asserted here. Source-verified 19 October 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-N6: “On an Invoiced or Paid work order the Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician action (S3-R14) and the Unassign action are disabled, and their tooltip reads “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” or “Paid · can’t be reassigned”, as in the design. The same words are the tooltip on the card’s or row’s lock icon, and the note shown at the top of another technician’s column or group while the work order is dragged over it, where the drop is refused.”
  • S4-N7: “Visually indicate that an Invoiced or Paid work order can only be reordered within its current technician, not moved to another one.”
  • S4-N2: “Do not allow the lead technician to change in Invoiced or Paid status. An Invoiced or Paid work order can still be dragged to reorder it within its current technician (or within Unassigned), but it cannot be moved to another technician, to Unassigned, or out of Unassigned. Declined and Complete work orders can be moved freely, as today.”

Not yet checked against a build in this wording.
